title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Σ is a bounded lattice with 0, 1 and an orthocomplementation C (an involutive, order-reversing map with b ∨ Cb = 1 and b ∧ Cb = 0), i.e. an ortholattice. The notation x|0|y means 'x and y are disjoint/orthogonal', i.e. x ≤ Cy. The page works out when pairs of elements behave classically, meaning they generate Boolean subalgebras.

Lemma 1. Take b ≤ c. The following are equivalent:
(i) b has an orthogonal relative complement in [0,c]: there is b* ⟂ b with b ∨ b* = c.
(ii) b ∨ (Cb ∧ c) = c.
Any such b* satisfies b* ≤ Cb ∧ c, so b0* = Cb ∧ c is the largest one. This is exactly the orthomodular law (Husimi), stated for a single pair b ≤ c.

Lemma 2. Take b ≤ c. The following are equivalent:
(i) b and c generate (under ∨, ∧, C) a Boolean subalgebra.
(ii) That subalgebra is finite of order 2^n with n ∈ {1,2,3}. The NB records the cases: n = 1 iff {b,c} ⊂ {0,1}; n = 2 iff b = 0, or c = 1, or b = c (and not n = 1); n = 3 iff 0 < b < c < 1.
(iii) Lemma 1 holds for the pair (b,c) and also for the dual pair (Cc, Cb).
(iv) Set α = b, β = c ∧ Cb, γ = Cc. Then α, β, γ are pairwise orthogonal and form a partition of unity, expressed by relative-complement equations such as C(γ∨α) = β and Cα ∧ (γ∨α) = γ. The atoms of the subalgebra are then α, β, γ.

Corollary. For an ortholattice Σ the following are equivalent:
(i) Lemma 1 holds for every pair b ≤ c, i.e. Σ is orthomodular. Grothendieck marks this as '(plus faible)', apparently a priori weaker.
(ii) Lemma 2 holds for every pair b ≤ c.
(iii) Any two orthogonal α, β generate a Boolean subalgebra, of order 2^n with n ≤ 3: n = 1 iff α, β ∈ {0,1}; n ≤ 2 iff α or β is 0; n = 3 iff α ≠ 0, β ≠ 0 and α ∨ β ≠ 1.
He then starts a version of (iii) for finite pairwise-disjoint families (α_i), which in an orthomodular lattice generate a Boolean algebra with atoms α_i and C(∨α_i). This step is left unproved.

Purpose. The previous pages concern 'spaties' (realisation |·|, a complement operation C, contractibility). This page seems to test which lattice-theoretic axioms on a 'complement' operation C make pairs and families of 'parts' behave Boolean. That is precisely the basic theory of orthomodular lattices.
errors: Lemma 1 (i) ⇒ b* ≤ Cb ∧ c needs '|0|' to mean orthogonality (b* ≤ Cb), not merely b ∧ b* = 0. In a non-distributive ortholattice, b ∧ b* = 0 does not imply b* ≤ Cb. With the orthogonal reading the lemma is correct.
The NB case analysis was heavily rewritten. The final version (n = 2 iff b = 0 or c = 1 or b = c, outside the n = 1 case) is correct.
In (iv), the list 'b, α, β, γ' should be just α, β, γ. One relation is transcribed as C(α∧β) = γ but must be C(α∨β) = γ.
Corollary (iii) and the finite-family statement are only sketched; no proofs are given on the page.

ideas.what: Existence of an orthogonal relative complement of b in [0,c] is equivalent to b ∨ (Cb ∧ c) = c; Cb ∧ c is the largest such complement
ideas.usually_credited_to: K. Husimi (1937); Birkhoff–von Neumann (1936) for quantum logic; systematised by Foulis, Holland, Kalmbach

ideas.what: A comparable pair b ≤ c generates a Boolean subalgebra (of order 2, 4 or 8) iff the orthomodular condition holds for (b,c) and the dual pair (Cc,Cb), iff the partition α, β, γ is orthogonal
ideas.modern_name: comparable/orthogonal elements are compatible (commute) and generate Boolean subalgebras; Foulis–Holland-type results

ideas.what: Characterisation of orthomodular ortholattices: every comparable pair, equivalently every orthogonal pair, generates a Boolean subalgebra; extension to finite orthogonal families
ideas.modern_name: characterisation of orthomodularity via Boolean blocks
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard orthomodular lattice theory (Foulis, Holland, Kalmbach)

missed.claim: In July 1986, alongside his work on 'spaties', Grothendieck independently rederives the basic theory of orthomodular lattices (quantum logic). It is not documented that he ever engaged with this structure.
missed.quote: (ii) On a $b\vee b_0^*=c$, où $b_0^*=Cb\wedge c$ ... $\forall$ couple $\alpha\,\beta$ avec $\alpha|0|\beta$, $\alpha$ et $\beta$ engendrent une sous-algèbre de Boole
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest. It shows his 1986 'spaties' programme considering non-distributive, orthocomplemented lattices of parts. The mathematics itself is classical (Husimi, Foulis, Holland).

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard elementary theory of orthomodular lattices, rediscovered and correct but well known since 1937–1963. The only mildly notable point is the biographical fact that Grothendieck was working with such structures in 1986.
transcription_corrections: 'si on a $b'$ comme dans (i)' should read 'si on a $b^*$ comme dans (i)'.
'$C(\beta)(\gamma\vee\alpha)=\alpha$' is likely '$C(\gamma)\wedge(\gamma\vee\alpha)=\alpha$' or similar, with a missing ∧.
The braced phrase is likely '(les $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ étant deux à deux disjoints)' rather than '{dans α,β,γ sont disjoints}'.
The last line likely reads 'Condition (iii), mais avec familles finies $(\alpha_i)$, deux à deux disjoints'.
The page number in the header is 108 (archive) / 105 (Grothendieck's own numbering).
